passage: Hi everyone, thanks for coming to this short talk from the Green Campus Club. Today we want to introduce our new plan to reduce plastic waste on campus. Right now, students throw away about two hundred plastic cups every single day just from the cafeteria, so starting next month, the cafeteria will stop offering free plastic cups. Instead, we're encouraging everyone to bring a reusable bottle, and if you don't have one, you can buy a club bottle for just one hundred dollars, which is much cheaper than the store price. We're also setting up five new recycling stations around campus, near the library, the gym, and the main building. If your class collects the most recyclables by the end of the semester, you'll win a pizza party for twenty people. We really believe small changes like this can make a big difference, so please join us in making our campus greener.

options: To announce a new cafeteria menu
To recruit new club members only
To report the results of a survey
To introduce a plan to reduce plastic waste
explain_zh: 廣播一開始就說 to reduce plastic waste on campus,所以目的是介紹減塑計畫,和菜單、單純招募社員、公布問卷結果都無關。

passage: Welcome to the Riverside Art Museum audio guide for our Impressionist Paintings exhibition. You are now standing in front of Room 3, which holds twelve paintings created between eighteen seventy and eighteen ninety. To your left is the museum's most famous piece, a painting of a garden in soft morning light, painted by a French artist in eighteen seventy-four. Notice how the artist used small, quick brushstrokes instead of smooth lines, which was a new style at the time and shocked many art critics. Feel free to get close to see the brushstrokes, but please do not touch the paintings. When you're ready, press the green button on your device to hear about the next painting, a river scene painted just two years later. The exhibition continues in Room 4, where you'll find paintings from a slightly later period. This guide will take about thirty minutes to complete if you listen to every stop.

passage: Welcome, first-year students, to Kingsbridge University. Over the next hour, I'll walk you through what to expect during your first semester. Registration for courses opens this Thursday at nine in the morning, and popular electives tend to fill up within a day, so I strongly recommend logging in right when the system opens rather than waiting until the evening. Each student is assigned an academic advisor, whose job is to help you plan a balanced schedule and answer any questions about degree requirements. You'll find your advisor's name and office hours on the student portal by tomorrow afternoon. In terms of housing, students living in dormitories must move in by the Saturday before classes begin, while those living off campus should still attend the mandatory safety briefing that same weekend. Finally, orientation week ends with a welcome fair on Sunday, where over eighty student clubs will have booths, so it's a great chance to explore your interests beyond the classroom.

options: To announce a change in tuition fees
To help new students prepare for their first semester
To explain how to apply for graduation
To recruit students for a research project
explain_zh: 講者整段都在說明第一學期要注意的事項,所以目的是幫新生做好準備,和學費調整、申請畢業、招募研究計畫都無關。

passage: Good morning, fellow students. My name is Alex, and I'm running for student council president this year. If elected, my main goal is to improve communication between the council and the student body, because right now, most students only hear about decisions after they've already been made. I plan to hold monthly open forums where anyone can raise concerns directly with council members, starting from the very first month of my term. I also want to address the cafeteria pricing issue that many of you have complained about, by negotiating directly with the school's catering company for at least a ten percent reduction on popular items. Lastly, I believe our school lacks enough quiet study spaces before exams, so I'll propose converting the unused room next to the library into a dedicated study hall by the end of the first semester. I know promises are easy to make, so I ask you to hold me accountable if elected. Thank you for listening, and I hope to earn your vote next week.

To present a candidate's election promises
To invite students to a school festival

passage: Thank you all for attending this briefing on our summer internship program. This year, we're offering forty positions across five departments, including marketing, finance, and product design. The program runs for eight weeks, from the third week of June through the second week of August, and interns will receive a monthly stipend of fifteen thousand dollars to help cover living expenses. Unlike previous years, this program is open to both third and fourth-year students, though priority will be given to those graduating within the next twelve months. To apply, you'll need to submit a resume and a short video introduction by the end of this month; there is no written test this year, which is a change from our usual process. Successful applicants will be notified by email within three weeks of the application deadline, and interviews will be conducted online rather than in person. We've found that about one in five interns receives a full-time job offer afterward, so this is a genuine opportunity worth considering seriously.
stem: What is this briefing mainly about?
explain_zh: 講者一開始就說 this briefing on our summer internship program,所以主旨是暑期實習計畫說明,和工讀博覽會、獎學金申請、研究所招生都無關。

A: That's really common. We usually pair people based on shared interests as well as language goals, so it doesn't feel like a formal lesson. Do you have any hobbies you'd like to talk about?

A: Either is fine, some pairs prefer a café instead, since it's more relaxed. I'll send you her contact details today, and you two can arrange the details yourselves.
B: Sounds great, thank you for setting this up.

options: To pair someone up for a language exchange partner
To register someone for a formal language class
To organize a hiking club event
